checks.command: Compare existing completed lexical and semantic profiles across exact option reversal at three existing caps, separately for sparse and richer sources
checks.result: 168 pair comparisons across 336 completed profiles; shared pair hashes confirm the same 14 underlying target pairs. Lexical rendered context is unchanged in all 84 comparisons. Semantic context changes in 5/42 sparse and 9/42 richer comparisons.

checks.command: Root integration replay using frozen f6 render_content and actual saved passages
checks.result: Independently rendered all 336 profiles, recomputed all 168 equality and exact-span comparisons, and rehashed 880 artifact pins. Five semantic changes only reorder the same passage multiset; nine change exact-span membership or boundaries. Published richer projections hash all 450 document identifiers.

checks.command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . on role05 branch

limitations: This is a descriptive diagnostic of saved retrieval context, not a scoring analysis or independent execution audit.
At the selected scaling cap of 8192 canonical UTF-8 bytes, reversed options change semantic context in 4/14 sparse pairs and 6/14 richer pairs. Lexical context is unchanged in both conditions.
Comparisons across caps, methods and source conditions reuse the same 14 underlying judgments from two researchers and three source groups; they add no independent target observations.
No prediction results or private labels were examined. Context changes do not establish the cause or existence of prediction flips, nor whether a change helps or harms accuracy.
When retrieval context also changes, the comparison measures pipeline-level option-order sensitivity and does not isolate consumer-only position sensitivity.
Exact-span differences include truncation-boundary changes; Jaccard is not semantic similarity.
These findings do not establish a general difference between sparse and richer sources. Current profiles, queries, embeddings, scaling selection and runtime remain frozen and unchanged.
